tasks.short: Assess soft tissue, joints, strength and range of motion

steps.what: Assess soft tissue condition, joint function, muscle strength and range of motion with the client

tasks.design: Keep physical assessment with the therapist. Existing notes in the {OTHER} clinical record system provide context without implying that software can perform palpation or assess joint quality.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assessment depends on touch, observation and the client's responses.
tasks.enabler_now: Documentation tools do not replace the physical examination.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting findings and recognising when referral is needed.
tasks.human_edge: Careful hands-on assessment and attention to discomfort and consent.
tasks.altitude: Assessment time and professional scope are unchanged.

reach.task: Assess a concern outside massage therapy scope

evidence.claim: Retaining physical soft-tissue and joint assessment is an E1 judgement; scribe capabilities do not demonstrate examination automation.

assumptions: Boundary is physical assessment, excluding separately performed documentation and treatment.
Therapist elicits symptoms and examines the client during fully retained s1; no structured condition flag or automated diagnosis is assumed.
No new system means zero incremental upkeep; existing software runtime is not a labour saving.
unknowns: Therapist scope and client assessment requirements
research_questions: Which findings require referral rather than continued massage assessment?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100; gross0 and net0. Hands-on assessment remains intact.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult other healthcare professionals on client treatment plans

steps.what: Prepare relevant client records and the consultation question, checking permission to share
Consult healthcare professionals and agree suitable treatment planning within each professional's scope

tasks.design: Use a native export in the {OTHER} clinical record system to prepare selected facts in {DOCS}. The therapist checks the question, sharing authority and exact material before consultation; collaborative treatment judgement remains human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Consultation preparation can require repeated copying of existing record details.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record templates can assemble selected information without generating clinical advice.
tasks.still_hard: Integrating different professional perspectives and deciding what is appropriate for the client.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining clinical context and recognising professional limits.
tasks.altitude: Less consultation-pack assembly; no new treatment-planning authority.

evidence.claim: Native clinical record export can reduce repeated copying; the saving and design here are E1 assumptions, not scribe-study results.
Health data is special-category personal data under GDPR Article 9.

assumptions: Boundary includes therapist preparation and consultation, excluding the other professional's unchanged consultation time and original clinical recording.

Therapist produces consultation question, relevant record selection, client identifier, recipient and sharing basis in s1's twelve retained hours. Missing permissions or facts are resolved manually there; no inferred diagnosis or treatment code is supplied free.
Exact pack and recipient approval occurs in fully retained s2 before any sharing. Native export is tested before custom work; consultation remains a person-to-person activity.
Two incremental therapist hours per 100 baseline hours cover template and access checks.
unknowns: Record export features, sharing arrangements and consultation preparation effort
research_questions: Does selected-record export save time after relevance and permission checks?

approvals.approved_version: Exact consultation material, client identity, recipient and sharing purpose; changes void approval
